reason: H0 only calls plist_from_bin and plist_free, while the source change is confined to binary-plist writing logic. Consequently, H0 does not execute the changed serialization paths, including their buffer offsets, byte swapping, and append lengths for real and date values.
evidence: H0 invokes only plist_from_bin(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data), size, &root_node) followed by plist_free(root_node).
write_real now writes into buff+7/buff+8 and calls byte_array_append(bplist, buff+7, size+1).
write_date now writes into buff+7/buff+8 and calls byte_array_append(bplist, buff+7, 9).
No operation in H0 serializes a plist node or deliberately supplies real/date node semantics to write_real or write_date.
recommended_action: Add writer-side fuzz coverage that serializes plist structures containing real and date values, varying floating-point bit patterns and structure context; optionally parse the resulting bytes again to validate the writer-to-parser protocol.
